thread:
Anika: Opening thread for route_profile_v2 rollout options. main goal: make console queries for route metadata fast and stable while avoiding a big dashboard migration. collecting tradeoffs here.
Ravi: quick note: current envelope scan dominates console route fetch p99 when tenants have many routes. v2 should denormalize hot fields used in filters.
Tess: Agree. We should list the exact hot fields (route_id, owner_team, quota_tier, retention_policy, tag_set) so we don't over-normalize.
Jordan: Two main migration patterns: adapter-only (read-time mapping from v1->v2 shape) or dual-write with eventual backfill. Adapter reduces writer changes but may hurt p99.
Dmitri: I'd add a hybrid: dual-write for new edits + adapter fallback for legacy rows. That reduces backfill pressure while giving reads a chance to prefer v2.
Anika: We sketched similar but need concrete performance guardrails. propose: if adapter adds >10ms median or >25ms p99 to route lookup, we flip to dual-write strategy.
Ravi: How do we measure that safely? suggest a canary route lookup endpoint /internal/route-lookup-profiler that returns timings and path used (v1/v2/cache). instrument and run 24h on staging and 2h on prod canary.
Tess: cache invalidation: with denorm table we can keep a tiny in-memory LRU per console instance keyed by route_id with TTL 30s. on route edit events we publish simple invalidation messages via pubsub.
Jordan: dashboards: many Grafana panels expect nested JSON fields. we can't edit them all. options: (1) create a compatibility view that projects v2 rows into the old envelope shape (2) populate a materialized table via CDC that matches existing panels.
Dmitri: CDC -> materialized table seems faster for dashboard queries. We can reuse our existing Kafka+Debezium path and write into analytics.route_profile_mv. Low-latency reads for dashboards, slightly increased infra complexity.
Anika: Backfill strategy question: full synchronous backfill vs streaming backfill workers. I prefer streaming workers with tenant-scoped rate limits and per-region windows to avoid IO spikes.
Ravi: include back-pressure: workers should watch Postgres bloat and API p99 and back off. Ops SIG should own kill-switch that pauses backfill per cluster.
Tess: Quota engine impact: quota buckets are derived from route attributes. during rollout, ensure quota reads consult canonical_source flag. proposal: maintain canonical= v1 until flip, but have quota engine read adapter that prefers v2. record shadow metrics.
Jordan: Reconciliation: run daily diff job comparing computed quota keys from v1 vs v2, emit anomaly alerts if >0.5% divergence, and reconsile by applying idempotent counter corrections via an internal admin job.
Dmitri: Tests: unit tests for adapter mapping, integration tests for console fetch with both v1 and v2 present, load test backfill at 2x expected throughput on staging, and dashboard query perf tests against materialized view.
Anika: Monitoring set: route_lookup_p50/p95/p99, adapter_hit_rate, dual_write_error_rate, cdc_lag_ms, mv_refresh_latency, backfill_bytes/s, quota_drift_rate. Dashboards for these must be created before canary.
Ravi: UX: console should surface migration_state per-tenant in admin panel. banner copy: "Route metadata migration in progress; some metrics may be delayed or incomplete." link to migration status page.
Tess: Schema ops: add schema_version integer column to route_profile_v2 and a last_updated_ts. follow compatibility rules: additive-only for minor versions, and full migration for breaking changes. document in repo.
Jordan: Rollout plan: 1) schema+table creation (no writers) 2) enable dual-write feature flag behind tenant opt-in 3) adapter in read layer (prefer v2) 4) small canary (5% tenants) + monitor 24h 5) CDC materialized view for dashboards 6) phased backfill 25% -> 50% -> 100% 7) flip canonical to v2 8) cleanup v1 paths after 4 weeks.
Dmitri: Can we automate tenant canary selection? pick based on low traffic and representative schema (no extreme edge cases). store canary list in migration-control table.
Anika: Good. Also include an emergency rollback: feature flag off should make producers stop writing v2 but reads still may prefer v2; ensure adapter can be toggled. document rollback steps.
Ravi: Security: new table must have same row-level access policies as envelopes and be SCB encrypted at rest. confirm with security.
Tess: I'll open a PR template with checklist items and required approvals: eng-platform, infra, security, prod-analytics, console.
Jordan: Who owns the Debezium wiring? ops-team + eng-platform. Need a maintenance window for initial MV population.
Dmitri: I can draft the backfill worker and reconciler. estimate 3 sprints to reach canary if we parallelize.
Anika: Action items summary: - Tess: PR template + banner copy + tests list - Ravi: route lookup profiler endpoint + monitor defs - Jordan: CDC MV plan + ops windows - Dmitri: backfill worker + reconciler - Anika: migration control table + schema docs.
ci-bot: Created task MIGRATE-72 "route_profile_v2: prepare schema and canary" and assigned to the group.
Anika: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene Friday 9am to lock windows and owners.
